title: Python: N-6, a conditional star after an unconditional def gives x.f alone (DEC-303 (a62) item 6, found in GCLI-118)
description: DEC-303 (a62) item 6, N-6, found in the GCLI-118 review (landed in opum-ai/glyph-cli#198, b3fd5d3e). Predates #198. A module-level 'from x import *' inside an if or try arm AFTER an unconditional def or class f of the module is treated by starOverride (src/python/calls.ts) as unconditionally deciding, giving x.f alone where Python gives x.f or m.f (an alternative under (a10) Q2 and (a61) item 2). starOverride reads stars from starBindingsByPath, which records no condition (the same limit resolveStarAttribute names: a star's try/except condition is ignored). Fold into the may-skip rule for stars. Wrong-edge class; joins the (a49) item 7 hold list; lands before the freeze.

acceptanceCriteria.text: m.py def f then a conditional star (if C: from x import *) with x exporting f: both forms give an edge to every alternative, each multiplyBound, or no edge, never x.f alone; red before and green after with callees pinned and the full bin delta
twins: an unconditional star after the def still decides x.f; a conditional star BEFORE the def is overridden by the def
a mutant that treats the star as unconditional is observed red
the five-pin corpus diff against dev is script-asserted with every moved site named; any in-repo edge created or removed comes to opum-doc before the clear

finalSummary: Landed in opum-ai/glyph-cli#202 (2096450b). A star that may be skipped (the maySkipStatement rule, recorded on the module scope) is a may-skip alternative: the star's symbols plus what the rest of the module decides, each multiplyBound; a non-symbol rest or an earlier live star is a refusal. A one-symbol union collapses to a symbol only when no outcome in it was multiply (DEC-303 (a65)). Fixtures in both forms red on the base, mutants observed red, five-pin corpus byte-identical. Opus round 1 and 2 requested changes, resolved by arm A of (a65). GCLI-127 filed for the attribute form's resolveStarAttribute.
